name: Thyssenkrupp Automotive Systems of America
old_description: As a publicly listed company, thyssenkrupp is part of the MDAX index. thyssenkrupp shares are traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: TKA) and as American depositary receipts (ticker symbol: TKAMY) in the USA. Since 20 October 2025, TKMS (Marine Systems segment) has also been an independent, publicly traded company in which thyssenkrupp AG holds a majority stake of 51 per cent; TKMS shares are traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: TKMS) and will be included in the MDAX from 22 December 2025.
about:
Thyssenkrupp Automotive Systems of America operates from Chattanooga, Tennessee, as part of the publicly traded thyssenkrupp AG, which is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and included in the MDAX index. The division traces its roots to the broader thyssenkrupp group’s automotive technology activities, though a specific founding year for the U.S. entity is not publicly disclosed. Ownership remains with the German parent company, and no individual founders are named for this subsidiary.

The company supplies high‑tech components and services to the automotive sector, covering drivetrain, undercarriage, body, and steering systems. Its portfolio includes forged and machined parts such as crankshafts, camshafts, cylinder head modules, damping systems, springs, stabilizers, and complete drive and battery assemblies. It also provides production systems for powertrain and battery lines, integrated car‑body solutions, engine and axle assembly, and development of electromechanical steering systems. The Chattanooga location employs approximately 28,892 people across the automotive technology segment, though facility size and annual volumes are not specified.

Customers are primarily automotive OEMs and tier‑1 suppliers in the passenger‑vehicle and commercial‑vehicle markets, as well as manufacturers of construction machinery. The company’s components serve chassis, body, and powertrain applications, with specific references to undercarriage systems, steering gears, and battery assembly for electric vehicles.

Thyssenkrupp highlights its steer‑by‑wire development approach, the use of artificial neural networks to improve steering‑gear quietness, and the cloud‑based IoT platform carValoo for real‑time fleet monitoring as key differentiators. The division positions itself as an integrated partner for production systems and component innovation.
